meta.name: Jay BIPU Content Idea Tournament
meta.pain_first_rule: An idea can only win by demonstrating the reader's pain more precisely than its opponent. Solution quality scores nothing until pain recognition scores.
meta.provenance: Pods seeded from Jay Yang's copywriting essay (docs/jay-yang-copywriting-article.md) and the live grader rubric.

format.round1: Within each pod, ideas face off pairwise; winners advance.
format.final: Pod champions meet in cross-pod bracket judged by all archetypes.
format.scoring: Each judge returns pain_recognition (0-5), specificity (0-5), action_pull (0-3). Pain recognition is weighted double and gates: if tied or losing on pain recognition, an idea cannot win regardless of other axes.
format.tiebreak: Higher pain_recognition, then higher specificity, then earlier seed order.

champion.text: You don't have a time problem, you have a key-man problem: everything routes to you because you never built a process that survives your absence.
Flat revenue for two quarters isn't a market condition. It's an unnamed bottleneck that everyone is quietly working around instead of naming.
Your product isn't underperforming. Your explanation of it loses to worse products with better sentences.
Likes are not pre-orders. An audience that applauds but doesn't buy is telling you the proof layer is missing, not the promise.
The most dangerous line in your financial plan is the one that assumes your employer keeps paying you.
